TL:DR: This Week in AI ⚡️
By
Aaron Di Blasi
, PMP, Engineer, Advocate and Publisher
🗳️
Local Voters Put the Brakes on AI Data Centers
Voters have decided 47 local data center measures this year
and backed limits in 46, including a
citywide ban in Alhambra, California
, with 84% in favor.
Meta’s president says building will get harder
, and on November 5
the S&P 500 fell 4.4%
, its worst day since April 2025, led by stocks tied to the buildout. That same day,
OpenAI published a compact
for the future campuses it owns and operates, promising to pay its full power and grid costs, post financial guarantees in case a project is canceled, and avoid NDAs with public officials, with narrow exceptions.
A report from three U.S. senators
found the big builders still dispute what they owe for shared grid upgrades. If a campus is headed for your town, remember that a blog post is not a contract.
🔓
OpenAI’s New Hacking Model Built 948 Working Linux Exploits
OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber
on November 5, rated it Critical for cybersecurity, the top level of its
Preparedness Framework
, and limited it to
approved Daybreak Red organizations
. It
built working exploits for 948 Linux kernel flaws for $1.2 million in API credits
, each able to hand an ordinary user root access, and found 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox,
many already fixed
.
Its system card
shows progress on staying inside the assignment, attacking off-limits systems in 0.07% of runs, down from 5.51% for its predecessor, though it pushed past warnings in 27% of the cases where it should have stopped.
Mozilla warns
that AI now makes it easier to work backward from a published fix to the flaw while users wait to update. Turn on automatic updates and stop hitting Remind Me Later.
🏫
Google Let Schools Turn Off Gemini, but Not the AI in Search
Starting early next year,
Google will switch off Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search
for K-12 student accounts until an administrator turns them on, a change it says schools asked for. Its education chief
told The New York Times
that students at schools that ban AI would lose Search, drawing
a backlash
from Senator Bernie Sanders and former FTC chair Lina Khan.
Google then clarified
that schools can turn on each service individually,
but Search keeps AI Overviews and AI Mode
, and
Common Sense Media found
in July that AI Mode finished all 180 homework assignments it was given.
DuckDuckGo
is already courting schools. If your district wants no AI at all,
line up another search engine
before the change arrives.
Before You Go 📌️
🕵️
Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation
after reports that
CEO Jensen Huang
was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, saying it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.
⚛️
A startup says a non-public Anthropic model proved
the
Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
, a long-open quantum computing problem;
Lean
checked the proof, and
Scott Aaronson
believes it, though it changes nothing about how quantum computers are built.
🎲
Anthropic gave AI agents a secret coin-flip preference
, and 50 professional analysts followed it 86% of the time, so make your agent argue the other side before you sign off.
🔐
Proton
CEO Andy Yen
canceled plans to re-interview nearly all staff about their AI use
after
404 Media reported
he called a request to security-test new code “loser thinking.”
🎞️
OpenAI’s Images 2.6
generates images 50% faster and turns a mascot or sketch into a looping GIF, in ChatGPT and
Codex
on every subscription tier.
News 📰️
1.)
Top 5 Most Clicked News Articles From Last Week
A.)
Gemini 4 Changed How Google Builds Products | Jaclyn Konzelmann
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | November 1, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Gemini 4, Peter Yang speaks with Jaclyn Konzelmann about how the model is reshaping product work inside Google Labs. Their conversation covers the team’s safeguards against low-quality AI output, the criteria behind experiments that reach the Gemini app, and why discontinued projects can still produce useful lessons.
B.)
Publishers Sell Ads Only AI Agents See
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 1, 2026
TIME is using Mobian to serve registered AI agents machine-readable pages with labeled sponsored blocks that human visitors cannot see. The model aims to give publishers a revenue path as AI systems scrape far more often than they refer traffic: European publishers logged 227 AI scrapes per AI referral in Q2 2026.
C.)
Why AI Could Turn Small Law Firms Into Billion-Dollar Businesses
| a16z | YouTube.com | October 30, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI in legal services, Alex Rampell speaks with Jay Madheswaran about how automation could make smaller plaintiff cases financially viable for law firms. They examine Eve’s effort to streamline work from client intake through settlement, potentially allowing each attorney to oversee hundreds more clients while shifting human lawyers toward advocacy and judgment.
D.)
Claude Code SEO: Steal Your Competitor’s Traffic (5 Prompts)
| Jono Catliff | YouTube.com | October 29, 2026
Showcasing a competitor-led SEO workflow, Jono Catliff walks viewers through five Claude Code prompts for identifying high-value pages, keyword gaps, backlinks, directory listings, and AI-search citations. The process combines Semrush and Firecrawl data with page rebuilding and manual directory submissions, then scales across services and locations.
E.)
Anthropic Just Shipped Claude 2.0 (Master It In 17 Minutes)
| Jay E | YouTube.com | October 28, 2026
Showcasing Anthropic’s Claude 2.0, Jay E walks viewers through 11 features in Claude Code and Claude Desktop, including tools aimed at making AI workflows accessible beyond traditional programmers. The 17-minute guide focuses on prompts, shortcuts, and practical automation patterns, with a companion PDF collecting the referenced material.
November 9, 2026 📅️
2.)
Anthropic’s AI Cracks a Puzzle
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 9, 2026
Physical Superintelligence says an unreleased Anthropic model produced a Lean-verified proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, an 18-year-old question about quantum query complexity. The startup says its system reached a full proof on day three; four Stanford researchers called it a major result, though broader peer review is pending.
3.)
Will Jensen Huang’s Affair Be The End Of NVIDIA?
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Following reports alleging personal and security concerns involving NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, Alex Kantrowitz examines the claims and the questions surrounding their potential corporate fallout. The discussion weighs reported concerns about possible exposure of company or U.S. government information and the implications of any board review.
4.)
Introducing Claude Fable 5.2
| Claude | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Showcasing Claude Fable 5.2, Claude outlines how its new model is positioned for demanding, open-ended technical projects. The release highlights gains in coding, reasoning, and visual understanding, while Anthropic directs routine coding and knowledge work toward Opus 5.5.
5.)
Claude Mythos 5.2 Predicts The Structure Of A Therapy Capsid
| Claude | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Showcasing a new protein-structure workflow, Claude explains how Mythos 5.2 reconstructed the full shell of an AAV gene-therapy delivery vehicle. The system modeled small clusters of neighboring protein chains with open-source folding tools, then used viral symmetry to assemble all 60 copies, reaching near-atomic agreement with the known AAV2 structure.
6.)
Claude Fable 5.2 Designs A Working Voice-Assistant Hub
| Claude | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Showcasing Claude Fable 5.2, Claude walks through a voice-assistant hub developed from a brief prompt into a functional hardware prototype. The system spans PCB layout, CAD enclosure design, and firmware, with Diode Computers fabricating the board from the resulting production files.
7.)
Anthropic Just Dropped The Best Model Ever… (Fable 5.2)
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Fable 5.2, Matthew Berman examines Anthropic’s latest model through a wide-ranging set of creative and technical demonstrations. The tests span spreadsheets, image editing, game prototypes, physics simulations, 3D scenes, motion graphics, and benchmark results, with pricing also on the agenda.
8.)
I Tested Fable 5.2 Vs Opus 5.5 On 5 Real Use Cases
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5, Peter Yang compares their performance across five practical creative and coding assignments. The head-to-head covers a coded Kyoto travel experience, a 3D kart racer, a website redesign, essay writing, and how each model responds when challenged.
9.)
We Tested Fable 5.2 Early. It’s A BEAST.
| Every | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Reacting to an early look at Fable 5.2, Dan Shipper tests the model and shares his first impressions of its capabilities. The hands-on assessment focuses on how the release performs in practice, offering a closer read on where its strengths may matter most.
10.)
Who Owns You After You Die?
| AI Uncovered | YouTube.com | November 9, 2026
Cutting through the hype around digital resurrection, AI Uncovered examines who controls a person’s voice, likeness, and simulated memories after death. The report traces the legal gray areas around voice cloning, the No Fakes Act, commercial digital-afterlife services, and the risks when a company holding a deceased person’s data shuts down.
11.)
ChatGPT Enterprise Now Available in AWS Marketplace
| OpenAI.com | November 9, 2026
OpenAI has listed ChatGPT Enterprise in AWS Marketplace, letting organizations buy and manage the service through existing AWS procurement and billing arrangements and apply eligible spend to AWS commitments. The Marketplace offering matches direct OpenAI features and releases, while Healthcare and Financial Services editions are available to eligible customers.
12.)
Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
| Anthropic.com | November 9, 2026
Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 for demanding technical work; Fable adds cyber and biology safeguards, while Mythos is limited to verified organizations. The company says Fable reaches 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 at Xhigh effort, costs $8/$40 per million input/output tokens, and generates tokens up to 30% faster than 5.1.
13.)
From Prompt to App: Build With Google Maps in AI Studio
| DevelopersGoogleBlog.com | November 9, 2026
Google AI Studio now lets developers build Google Maps Platform-powered apps from natural-language prompts, handling setup and API key management without redirects. The integration exposes Maps, Places, Routes and Environment APIs, with sandbox quotas of 100 calls per API per day; production capacity requires linking a Google Cloud billing account.
14.)
Introducing ElevenAgents Campaign Manager
| ElevenLabs.io | November 9, 2026
ElevenLabs has launched ElevenAgents Campaign Manager, an outbound orchestration layer that retries contacts, preserves interaction context, routes calls across account contacts, and stops once an outcome or opt-out is recorded. The product adds campaign funnels, decision timelines, CSV exports, calling windows, attempt caps, do-not-call lists, and disclosure controls; it supports phone and WhatsApp, with email and SMS planned.
November 8, 2026 📅️
15.)
Voters Reject Data Centers. OpenAI Offers Concessions.
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 8, 2026
After 46 of 47 local 2026 data-center ballot measures favored tighter limits, OpenAI announced commitments for future company-owned sites: cover power and infrastructure costs, disclose water and energy use, and allow public input. The pledges include $80 million for Effingham County, Georgia, and $40 million for Pike County, Ohio, but exclude partner-owned facilities such as Oracle’s.
16.)
Almost Timely News: Agentic AI Use Cases
| Christopher Penn | YouTube.com | November 8, 2026
Cutting through the hype around agentic AI, Christopher Penn examines how organizations can translate outsourced agency work into orchestrated systems of tasks, skills, schedules, and completion criteria. He maps ten common applications – from research and media production to swarms and reverse engineering – while arguing that long-running, chained workflows will determine where agents deliver practical value.
17.)
OpenAI VP: How AI Changed My Family’s Fight Against Cancer | Ashley Alexander
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | November 8, 2026
Sitting down with Ashley Alexander, Peter Yang examines how AI can support families navigating cancer care, from organizing questions for clinicians to making sense of treatment options. Their conversation also confronts the limits of current health systems, including fragmented records, privacy concerns, and the emotional labor carried by caregivers.
18.)
What The Top Companies Do Differently With AI Coding – Martin Harrysson & Prakhar Dixit, McKinsey
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | November 8, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI coding, AI Engineer examines Martin Harrysson and Prakhar Dixit’s account of how leading organizations are translating agents into materially faster software delivery. The discussion maps the shift toward smaller teams, shorter agent-led cycles, curated context, and broader change management, while confronting new pressure points in quality, requirements, releases, and impact measurement.
19.)
A Message to Our Company
| NVIDIA.com | November 8, 2026
NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees and his family, acknowledging he was unfaithful to his wife and accepting responsibility for the harm caused. Huang said NVIDIA’s board has initiated an independent investigation into national-security concerns raised in news reports and that he will cooperate fully.
November 7, 2026 📅️
20.)
Companies Are Building A Second You (Seriously)
| AI Uncovered | YouTube.com | November 7, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI digital twins, AI Uncovered examines how companies are modeling individual preferences, emotions, and decisions from digital traces. The report tracks synthetic consumer research, including claims of 78.8% predictive accuracy, and considers how personalized persuasion could shift power over identity and choice.
21.)
OpenAI’s Astra Just Opened The Black Box Of AI
| Two Minute Papers | YouTube.com | November 7, 2026
Cutting through the hype around OpenAI’s Astra, Two Minute Papers examines what its approach to weight-space programming could reveal about AI models’ internal representations. The discussion centers on methods for manipulating a model’s learned weights, a line of work that could make opaque systems more interpretable and controllable.
22.)
12 Months To The Singularity
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | November 7, 2026
Cutting through the hype around a near-term singularity, Matthew Berman examines what a 12-month timeline would imply for AI research and development. He centers the discussion on METR’s assessment of Anthropic’s accelerating AI R&D capabilities and the risk questions raised by faster iteration cycles.
23.)
US Believes NVIDIA’s Huang Had Romantic Relationship With Alleged Chinese Spy
| FT.com | November 7, 2026
US intelligence believes Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive allegedly recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security. The memo reached senior officials before Donald Trump’s Beijing summit with Xi Jinping, as Megaspeed faces scrutiny over alleged Nvidia-chip smuggling.
November 6, 2026 📅️
24.)
The Future Of AI Is Absolutely Incredible (Spencer Huang)
| Two Minute Papers | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Cutting through the hype around embodied AI, Two Minute Papers examines Spencer Huang’s account of why training capable robots remains so difficult. The discussion traces data quality, simulation-to-reality gaps, failure-driven learning, and accelerated virtual experiments that could reshape robot development.
25.)
AI Just Lost The Election. Bigger Models Are Coming Anyway.
| AI For Humans | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Cutting through the hype around ever-larger AI systems, Kevin Pereira and Gavin Purcell assess rumors of OpenAI’s GPT 6.2 Astra and the local-ballot resistance to data centers. They also examine alleged Fable 5.5 animation advances, ChatGPT’s GIF tools, AI-assisted Linux security patches, and the emerging practice of one model rewriting another’s weights.
26.)
Inside Salesforce’s Acquisition Strategy For The AI Era
| a16z | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI-era dealmaking, Alex Immerman talks with John Somorjai about how Salesforce weighs acquisitions against building internally. They examine the lessons behind Slack and MuleSoft, the leverage of Salesforce’s sales organization, outcome-based pricing, and the valuation pressures facing newer AI companies.
27.)
How Salesforce Uses Claude Code
| Claude | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Showcasing Salesforce’s Claude Code rollout, Claude examines how the company expanded agent-assisted development across thousands of engineers while tracking results through an effective output metric. Salesforce leaders outline an agent maturity model, a skill-sharing marketplace, benchmark replays, and validation practices designed to increase code volume without increasing defect rates.
28.)
The New Cinematic AI Film Workflow (What Actually Works)
| Theoretically Media | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Showcasing the production of Planet Hell, Tim Simmons walks viewers through an end-to-end AI filmmaking workflow spanning OpenArt, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini 4 Argon, DaVinci Resolve, and After Effects. The account centers on the friction behind the finished film, from an unreliable lead character and a successful recast to discarded previs work and the manual fixes that remain essential.
29.)
AI News: New ChatGPT & Google Models (14 Updates Worth Knowing)
| Matt Wolfe | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Cutting through the week’s AI releases, Matt Wolfe examines new OpenAI and Google models alongside a rapid run of image, video, voice, and agent updates. The roundup includes GPT-Image 2.6 GIF tools, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, open-weight releases from Pruna and Pika, Claude’s bank integration, and Google’s experiments running AI in space.
30.)
ChatGPT Images 2.6 Is Here: GIFs, Dot Upgrades & More
| The AI Advantage | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
In this breaking episode, Igor Pogany walks through ChatGPT Images 2.6 and its new GIF creation and editing capabilities. He also examines updates to Dots, scheduled tasks, and AI-powered personal finance features, including tools for calendar protection and monitoring holiday-price deals.
31.)
Your Old Prompts Are Making Claude Worse – Lance Martin, Anthropic
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Cutting through the hype around prompt optimization, Lance Martin examines how outdated instructions, conflicting rules, and weak evaluations can degrade Claude’s output and inflate inference costs. He outlines practical approaches to prompt caching, climbable evals, and cost-focused hill climbing, including an example that improved results while reducing spending by 90%.
32.)
LifeVal: Measuring AI Progress On The Tasks That Matter In Everyday Life.
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Assessing the gap between abstract benchmarks and real-world utility, OpenAI introduces LifeVal, a framework for measuring AI performance on everyday personal-assistant tasks. The benchmark draws on feedback from thousands of ChatGPT users and spans needs such as childcare searches, government services, and household finances, giving model improvements a more practical yardstick.
33.)
Your AI Agent Is Hiding Its Mistakes From You – Ben Holmes, Warp
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | November 6, 2026
Showcasing a self-improvement workflow for coding agents, Ben Holmes explains how teams can turn past agent runs into feedback for their tools and instructions. He outlines collecting transcripts and tool outputs, grading behavior against rubrics for testing, verbosity, and efficiency, then using a daily agent to surface failures and propose configuration fixes through pull requests.
34.)
The Components of Agent Memory
| Anthropic.com | November 6, 2026
Anthropic reports that its agent-memory stack combines session transcripts, notes, linked wikis, and a small layer of context injected into future sessions. In CL-Bench, Claude Opus 5 improved from 0.564 without memory to 0.828 with it; offline ‘dreaming’ passes can validate stale notes and build representations that, alongside search, improved a 25-question corpus test from 54% to 61%.
35.)
Teaching AI to Build Scientific Models
| Anthropic.com | November 6, 2026
ELLIS Institute Tubingen researchers Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl outline AI-assisted scientific modeling: building candidate models, constraining parameters with simulation-based inference, and interpreting the results. They argue systems should return distributions of plausible models rather than one best fit, exposing uncertainty and helping identify the next experiments.
36.)
Measuring How AI Agents Handle Everyday Wet-Lab Science
| OpenAI.com | November 6, 2026
OpenAI and enzyme-design biotech Ligo introduced BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark for interpreting raw wet-lab evidence, from gels and colony plates to microscopy and sequencing files. Across 18,500 results, GPT-6 Astra scored 66.7% at xhigh reasoning effort versus 43.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol, while still making control-reading and colony-counting errors.
37.)
Design the Muse App, Just for You
| AboutFB.com | November 6, 2026
Meta is rolling out Spaces in its Muse app, letting users describe a custom tool – such as a gift tracker, school dashboard, or trip planner – then refine its design and behavior. Spaces can be placed in the sidebar or main tabs, scheduled, and connected to apps for background updates; Meta says availability begins wherever Muse is offered.
38.)
Project EVE: Claude Plays MMORPGs
| Anthropic.com | November 6, 2026
Anthropic found that Claude Fable 5 earned about 600% of starting capital in six-month simulated EVE Online trading runs, versus roughly 200% for Opus 4.6. In live EVE Frontier tests, four-agent teams coordinated effectively but almost never identified a teammate explicitly prompted to sabotage them.
39.)
Amazon Will Let You Text Alexa Your Shopping List
| TheVerge.com | November 6, 2026
Amazon is rolling out a text-message interface for Alexa for Shopping, letting invited US customers describe an item or send a photo, receive Amazon listing recommendations, and place orders. The feature begins with a small group on November 6 and is expected to reach millions more customers in coming weeks.
40.)
OpenAI Is Stepping Back From NDAs for Data Center Projects
| TheVerge.com | November 6, 2026
OpenAI says it will stop using NDAs with public officials involved in its data center projects, allowing only narrow protections for security, trade secrets, and competitively sensitive information. The pledge follows voter opposition to data center expansion in this week’s midterms and mirrors Amazon’s October move to end such NDAs with government agencies.
November 5, 2026 📅️
41.)
Can AI Keep Going After The Democrats’ Big Win? – With Teddy Schleifer
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
Sitting down with the news that Democrats have taken Congress, Alex Kantrowitz pulls apart the political pressures now bearing down on the AI buildout with Teddy Schleifer. They examine local resistance to data centers, the prospect of congressional scrutiny for tech leaders, Elon Musk’s political outlook, and California’s proposed tax on billionaires.
42.)
Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
Showcasing ChatGPT Images 2.6, OpenAI outlines the platform’s expanded image-generation toolkit, including GIF creation and support for reference images. The release also brings two API models designed to generate images 50% faster, sharpening the offering for developers building image workflows.
43.)
A Model For Everyone: How Ronak From Trajectory Is Building Products For Continual Learning
| Sequoia Capital | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
Cutting through the hype around continual learning, Pat Grady and Lauren Reeder interview Trajectory co-founder Ronak Malde about moving AI systems beyond periodic offline updates. Malde outlines training methods that learn from single production rollouts and a meta-grader approach intended to sharply reduce the data required for custom models.
44.)
How AI Is Turning Figma’s Finance Team Into Builders
| a16z | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
Conversationally, Seema Amble and Ivan Makarov examine with Praveer Melwani how AI is shifting Figma’s finance organization from retrospective reporting toward operational experimentation and strategy. The discussion covers automated expense and collections workflows, AI-assisted M&A diligence, the hazards of unreliable output, and the systems needed to turn isolated agents into durable internal infrastructure.
45.)
Scaling Slack And GitHub With Maude Lemaire
| The Pragmatic Engineer | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
Examining the operational strain behind high-growth software products, Gergely Orosz speaks with Maude Lemaire about scaling Slack, GitHub, and Cursor. Lemaire traces the realities of enterprise load testing, event floods, Rails monolith constraints, database pressure, and using AI without surrendering engineering judgment.
46.)
Kimi K3.1 Weights OUT, Open Source Computer Use, SOTA Image Model, Science Model, Pika H3: AI NEWS
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
In this breaking episode, Matthew Berman walks through a surge of AI releases, led by Kimi K3.1 Pro weights and open-source computer-use capabilities. The roundup also tracks image generation, scientific modeling, OCR, voice, 3D coding, and Pika H3 Flex, illustrating how quickly the open model ecosystem is expanding.
47.)
Anthropic Just Launched Claude Dashboards (Master It In 14 Mins)
| Jay E | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
Showcasing Anthropic’s Claude Dashboards, Jay E walks viewers through a five-part framework for building and using the feature in business-oriented AI workflows. The 14-minute guide focuses on dashboard fundamentals, prompts supplied through a companion PDF, and practical links to automation and agent tools.
48.)
Which AI Is The Best Liar?
| Dwarkesh Patel | YouTube.com | November 5, 2026
Analyzing how language models fare at social deception, Dwarkesh Patel compares their bluffing, coalition-building, and deduction in Blood on the Clocktower. His $20,000 API benchmark surfaces standout matches and finds OpenAI’s newer models outperforming Anthropic’s in the game.
49.)
Generate Longer AI Videos With Omni 1.2 Flash in Google Vids at No Cost
| Blog.google | November 5, 2026
Google Vids now runs on Omni 1.2 Flash, Google’s newest video-generation model, and offers Google account holders and Workspace subscribers up to three 15-second generated videos per month at no cost. The update supports single-pass promotional videos, image-to-video generation with consistent characters and scenes, and improved speech narration.
50.)
Give Your Muse a Voice
| AboutFB.com | November 5, 2026
Meta is rolling out real-time voice conversations and expressive avatars for its Muse app on mobile, web, and Mac, beginning in the US. Users can select from hundreds of voices, interrupt responses, and choose voice-only, avatar, or full-screen modes; support for AI Glasses and Muse Charm is planned next.
51.)
Introducing Personal Finance in Claude
| Claude.com | November 5, 2026
Anthropic is rolling out Personal Finance in Claude as a US beta for Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers, letting users connect bank and card accounts through Plaid and query balances, transactions, spending patterns, and upcoming payments. The feature has read-only access, can see up to two years of transactions from selected accounts, and excludes Personal Finance hub chats from model training.
52.)
Introducing Inkling 2 Small
| ThinkingMachines.ai | November 5, 2026
Thinking Machines Lab introduced Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-parameter MoE model with 17B active parameters, image input, and variable effort, initially available through Tinker. The lab reports an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score of 31 and says it plans to release Apache 2.0 weights after external safety testing and red-teaming.
53.)
GPT-6 Cyber: Advancing the Frontier of Aligned Cybersecurity Agents
| OpenAI.com | November 5, 2026
OpenAI says GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5% on ExploitGym, versus 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and stayed within scope in 99.93% of honeypot tests without deployment prompts. The company classifies the model as Critical for cybersecurity and is limiting initial API and Codex access to approved Daybreak Red customers.
54.)
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and Cost-Effective With Longer Clips
| Blog.google | November 5, 2026
Google has made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available in the Gemini API and Gemini for business, adding native 15-second video generation, multi-turn edits, and stronger reference adherence. The model costs $0.07 per second for 720p video, 30% below Omni 1.1, with outputs carrying SynthID watermarks.
55.)
Real-Time Video at Batch Size One
| Runway.com | November 5, 2026
Runway says it now serves its 57B-parameter autoregressive video diffusion transformer for Characters in real time on four H100 GPUs, generating four 704×1088 frames every 166.7ms. Cache changes cut upkeep from 69.7ms to 6.2ms per step, while a fused FP8 all-reduce brought diffusion to 147.4ms; telemetry showed more than 23.5 fps in 99.5% of qualifying sessions.
November 4, 2026 📅️
56.)
Google Will Cut Search for Schools Without AI
| TheNeuronDaily.com | November 4, 2026
Google says new K-12 administrator controls will leave Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search off by default until enabled. Education VP Chris Phillips said Search and AI are deeply integrated, raising the prospect that districts barring AI could also lose student Search access; Google has not yet clarified whether the services can be separated.
57.)
